title: A Volcano Buried His City. His Prison Cell Saved Him: The Full Case of Ludger Sylbaris

authoring.run: scheduled long run, 20 Nov 2026 (second long run of the day; r023-herfkens-long is held by another run)

description:
Case 030, the full case file. In the spring of 1902 Mount Pelée, the volcano above the port of Saint-Pierre on Martinique, woke up: steam at the summit, tremors, then ash on the streets. Snakes driven off the slopes came into the town, and around fifty people died of their bites. On 5 May a mudflow came down a river valley and buried a factory on the coast with its workers. The town stayed: an election was due on Sunday 11 May, a commission reported on 7 May that Saint-Pierre was in no danger, villagers from the slopes came into town for safety, and the governor came with his wife. In the town jail was Ludger Sylbaris (also recorded as Louis-Auguste Cyparis), held after a fight. For slipping out overnight to a party and coming back in the morning he was put in solitary: a stone cell built partly underground, with no window and one narrow grating in the door. On 8 May, just before eight in the morning, a cloud of burning gas and ash swept down the mountain and over the town in minutes. Ships burned at anchor; one steamer, the Roddam, got away. Around 28,000 people died, the governor and his wife among them. Hot air and ash came through the grating and burned Sylbaris's back, arms and legs, though his clothes did not catch fire; he wet his clothing with his own urine and pushed it into the grating. Days later men from outside the town heard him shouting and dug him out. He was pardoned and toured America with Barnum and Bailey's circus in a copy of his cell, billed as the man who lived through Doomsday. The French geologist Alfred Lacroix studied the eruption and named the cloud a nuée ardente, a glowing cloud; a spine of rock hundreds of metres high grew in the crater and crumbled in 1903. Sylbaris died around 1929 in Panama. Saint-Pierre is a small town today, and his cell still stands in it.

Animated reconstruction of a true story, made with respect for the people of Saint-Pierre. Nobody who died is shown dying. The town, the quay, the lane, the factory, the commission's room, the carriage, the party, the prison, the cell, the ships, the circus and every person are generic low-poly reconstructions; no building is a model of the real one and no likeness is attempted. The circus bill and the card of dates are drawings made for this film. Staging details such as the fruit stall, the door pulled shut, who sat on the commission, the governor's arrival by carriage, the dancing, the look of the steamer, the shoemaker's workshop, the geologist's notebook and camera, and everything Rook does are reconstruction, not record. Sources disagree on several figures (the dead: 27,000 to 30,000; the mudflow's victims: 23 or about 150; the rescue: the third or the fourth day; the height of the spine: about 270 to 340 metres), so the film says 'around 28,000', gives no number for the mudflow, says 'days' and says 'hundreds of metres'. Narration is a synthetic voice (Kokoro).

experiments.spine: Long-form spine v2: cold open on the cloud burying the city, Rook's doubt at the cell door with the burning sky behind him, then back to the start (the long-form convention of r001-okene-long and r024-alkemade-long) and forward in order. Date, place and names are on-screen labels.
experiments.learnings_applied: plan/learnings.json asks long-form for a shorter setup and a stronger mid-video reversal. The setup (town, warnings, why the town stayed, why he was in solitary) is seven segments of 4 to 13 s, each with its own event, and the eruption arrives at 41% of the runtime as the re-hook ('Then comes the eighth of May'); the reversal ('And here's the turn. The cell built to punish him is the only reason he's alive') lands at 71%.
experiments.rook_action: Detective actions in the story world: at the summit he looks down at the town from the steam (9); he points out the smoking mountain behind the commission (17); he raps the cell wall and sizes up the slit (26); he listens at the slit (40); he lays his wing on the wall that saved him (51); he reads the geologist's notes (57). Mannerisms: coin flip (7, 8, 22), beak tap (9, 57), finger along the hat brim (10), hat off his head and a shed feather (11, 56), brim low and arms folded (4, 17, 27), hat off for the dead and the rescue (14, 43, 49), hat held on (39, 60), hat tip at the sign-off (66). His jokes stop at shot 12 for the deaths, come back only for the party and the cell test, and stop again from the eruption (shot 28) until the pardon.

sound_plan.music: The engine's score follows the segment moods: hook; tense for the doubt; calm for the town; tense for the warnings; action for the mudflow; tense for 'the town stays'; calm for his story; tense for solitary; calm for Rook's test; tense, then action for the eighth of May; tense in the cell; sad for the quiet and the dead (no drum loop); tense for the wait; triumph for the rescue; wonder for the turn, the pardon and the circus; calm for the science and the afterlife; end.
sound_plan.effects: One to four cues a shot, each tied to something visible: gulls and waves on the quay, ticks for the coin, scratches for the snakes and footsteps, a clunk for the shut door, a crash for the mud, drum hits at the party, booms and whooshes for the cloud, a horn for the steamer, a grab for the cloth, heartbeats in the dark, shouts at the slit, a flip for the paper, a crash as the spine breaks, a pop for the hat tip.
sound_plan.hush: Shot 49 (the door dragged open): the music drops out for the breath before the turn.
sound_plan.tragic_beats: Shots 12 to 14 and 28 to 49 carry no joke; Rook holds his hat in shots 14, 43 and 49.

source_notes: Method, and its limit: in this session (20 Nov 2026) the fetch tool could not open any page (the session's network settings block en.wikipedia.org, volcanoes.sdsu.edu, amusingplanet.com, atlasobscura.com and the rest), so nothing was read in full. Every fact the long version adds to the Short was checked through nine web searches whose results quote the pages listed in 'sources'; a fact was kept only when the extracts of at least two sites agreed, and worded no more precisely than they agree. The Short's own facts rest on the eight pages its run read in full on 18 Nov 2026 (see episodes/r030-sylbaris/episode.json). Added facts and where the extracts agree: warning signs from April, steam vents, tremors, ash on the town in early May (Earth magazine, History.com, Wikipedia; dates of the first ash differ between 1 and 3 May, so the card says EARLY MAY). Snakes and insects driven into the town, about fifty people dead of snakebite (Wikipedia, the French Wikipedia article, SDSU, Lost in History). A mudflow down the Riviere Blanche on 5 May buried the Guerin works at the river mouth (Wikipedia, SDSU, Earth magazine, Volcano DB; one site dates it 2 May; 23 dead in most, about 150 in Wikipedia; sugar works in some, rum distillery in others, so the film says 'a factory', gives no number, and shows no person). Election due on Sunday 11 May (Wikipedia, Earth magazine and others; 11 May 1902 was a Sunday). A commission reported that the town was in no danger (Wikipedia, Earth magazine, two commentary sites; the label uses no quotation marks because the exact wording differs). Villagers from the slopes came into Saint-Pierre (Wikipedia, Volcano DB). Governor Louis Mouttet and his wife died in the town (Wikipedia's article on him, USGS chronology, others; her first name differs between sources and is not used; whether he tried to keep people in the town is disputed and is not claimed). The cloud crossed the town within one to three minutes at hundreds of kilometres an hour (figures from over 160 to about 670 km/h; the film says 'minutes' and 'hundreds of kilometres an hour'). Ships burned in the harbour and the steamer Roddam was the only one to get away, reaching Saint Lucia (Hartlepool history site, MaritimeQuest, Factinate, contemporary newspaper reports; 15 or 18 ships in harbour, not stated). He wet his clothing with his own urine and pushed it into the grating (Wikipedia, Atlas Obscura, Gizmodo, Forbes); the film says 'the only way he can' and does not show it. A shoemaker, Leon Compere-Leandre, at the edge of the town, also lived (Wikipedia, Amusing Planet, Scientific American blog; how he survived is told differently, so the film shows only a man coming out of a low workshop and the label does not name him). Barnum and Bailey's circus, a replica of his cell, billed as the man who lived through Doomsday (Wikipedia, Atlas Obscura, SDSU, Vintage News); the circus is named in the narration only, and no poster, logo or lettering of it is shown. Alfred Lacroix studied the eruption and introduced the term nuee ardente (Frontiers in Earth Science 2020, Britannica, Wikipedia). A lava spine grew from the crater from late 1902 and collapsed in 1903 (heights given from about 270 to 340 m; the film says 'hundreds of metres'). Sylbaris died about 1929 in Panama (Wikipedia, Vintage News and others; 'around 1929'). Saint-Pierre today has about 4,000 people (Wikipedia: 3,961 in 2023; one travel site: about 4,000); the film says 'a small town'. Left out because the extracts gave one source, disagreed, or were disputed: the claim that he was the first Black man to star in the circus (flagged 'citation needed'), the telegraph operator's last word, the name 'Paris of the Caribbean', the governor's motives, the exact day of the rescue, his age and trade, the girl who is said to have escaped by boat, the later eruptions of 20 May and 30 August 1902 and of 1929.

quality_gate.method: One run, three contact-sheet rounds and three full-length rehearsals. Rounds 1 to 3: low-res 16:9 contact sheets of every 3D shot (one frame each, 640x360). Found and fixed: Rook hidden behind another figure in four shots (the stall, the commission's window, the road, the geologist) and out of the wide frame in the rescue (he now sits on the edge of the pit); the commission tiny behind its table and the mountain filling the window with no smoke in view; the mudflow lost behind the valley's hills, and its aftermath too dark with Rook floating above the mud; the snake close-up mostly blank wall; the steam at the summit out of frame, then a puff over the lens at the start of the shot; the ship fires and the light on the steamer blown out, and the steamer too dark to read before that; the strip of light in 'the slit goes dark' not reaching his face; a camera inside a house wall in the third use of the cloud shot and inside the cell wall at the start of Rook listening; the rock spine and Rook too small. Rehearsals: every 3D frame at 480x270, 4 samples, 6 fps, composited at 1920x1080 and 30 fps with captions, labels, overlays, inserts and sound, reviewed as 2-frames-per-second strips of the 3D frames and tiles of the composite. Rehearsal 1 stopped at 37 s: the card of dates crashed on an empty text line (fixed), and the local gate flagged a slow first second and static stretches in the mud aftermath and the rock spine. Fixed by a strong push-in on the opening shot, a slight arc and push on every new shot, Rook taking his hat off during the mud aftermath, and a faster rise and fall of the spine; the board's text ran off the right edge (moved in); the sign-off card sat over Rook (moved right); the thumbnail still was framed from outside the cell door (re-staged inside). Rehearsal 2 PASSED the local gate; two shots of 3.5 s passed on thin motion margins, so the wait became two shots and the wide of the cell was shortened. Rehearsal 3 PASSED: 66 shots, mean 2.53 s, longest 4.64 s, first second motion 2.32 (minimum 2.0), Rook acting in 27 of 66 shots (41%), -14.6 LUFS, peak -1.2 dBFS, voice 16.1 dB over the bed, closest match to any earlier episode 0.85 (the card of dates against a card in r017-callahan-long; the limit is 0.93). Duration 167.0 s. After rehearsal 3 only the second view of the slit (shot 46) was re-angled and checked as a still. The cloud render runs the real gate at 1280x720 and 60 fps.
quality_gate.checked: Every kind in the storyboard exists in world3d.SHOTS3D (63 shots) or scenes.SHOTS (timeline, poster, board); HOST lists every kind in which Rook is placed; no kind is used more than three times (cloud_town three times, from three angles) and none twice in a row. First shot 1.9 s with a boom at 0.02 s. Re-hook ('Then comes the eighth of May') at 41% of the runtime; the turn at 71%. One hush shot (49). The thumbnail (his face in the slit light on the right, SAVED BY / HIS CELL on the left) was composed and looked at: the words are inside the frame and off the subject. Every on-screen label, the card of dates and the board were checked against the sources: SAINT-PIERRE, MARTINIQUE; SPRING 1902; APRIL 1902: MOUNT PELEE; ASH ON THE STREETS; SNAKES IN THE TOWN; ABOUT 50 DIED OF SNAKEBITE; 5 MAY 1902; THE COMMISSION: NO DANGER; INTO TOWN, TO BE SAFE; THE GOVERNOR AND HIS WIFE; LUDGER SYLBARIS; SOLITARY; ONE SLIT; 8 MAY 1902; JUST BEFORE 8 A.M.; A BURNING CLOUD; OVER THE TOWN IN MINUTES; THE RODDAM GETS AWAY; HIS CLOTHES DID NOT BURN; NO WATER; AROUND 28,000 DEAD; A SHOEMAKER, AT THE EDGE OF TOWN; DAYS PASS; DAYS LATER; PARDONED; ON TOUR ACROSS AMERICA; A COPY OF HIS CELL; ALFRED LACROIX, GEOLOGIST; NUEE ARDENTE: GLOWING CLOUD; A SPINE OF ROCK, 1902 TO 1903; DIED AROUND 1929 IN PANAMA; SAINT-PIERRE TODAY; THE CELL STILL STANDS. No death, no body, no wound and no bite is shown; the people of the town appear only alive, before the eruption.
quality_gate.not_met: Status is 'ready' (private), not 'approved', for one reason: no source page could be opened in this session (direct fetches are blocked by the session's network settings), so the facts added for the long version were checked against search-result extracts of at least two sites each, not against the full pages. No full-resolution, full-sample render was made locally (the workflow does it); motion was judged at 6 fps of 3D frames. The script runs 2 min 47 s, a little under the runbook's 3 minutes, because nothing else passed the two-source test. Three shots still move little (the second view of the geologist, Rook on the ledge in the cell, the shout at the slit); all are under 2.5 s. The low-poly cloud and mud read as stylised masses, not realistic flows. The human heads have no eyelids. The voice was measured, not listened to; the spoken form of 'nuee ardente' ('nway ar-dont') was not heard.
